title: The light chooses its vessel: the Names of Adam Kadmon, the three governors, and the tikunim
overview:
The chapter gives the *nimshal* of the soul in the body. The light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, as it comes from *Adam Kadmon*, is like the soul's intellect before the brain: one with its source, and its revelation only a color, like the apple's. Yet once G-d chooses a color it becomes essential, as wanting to help this person is bound to being nice. So in *Adam Kadmon* G-d chose to be wise, to create and to rule, though to Him all-knowing is no more a praise than "all-stupid", and the lights of the *sefiros* are still *b'li ma*.

These choices are the Names: *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*. Before *Atzilus* they are the source of the lights; after it, as the brain, the heart and the liver, they are the vessels made from the light's thickening, as a chair takes the shape of its sitter. So one should pray to the light, and the vessel follows. The vessels are also *tikunim*, like glasses for the eye or a uniform: they let the light come down, and let us see G-d without being burned.

terms.gloss: sefiros without a what: the lights of Atzilus, not yet defined, infinite compared to the vessels
the will for the will: the essential will connected to a particular will, which makes the particular essential
the names of the Emanator: the four Names of Adam Kadmon, the way G-d chose to reveal Himself
thickening: the end of the light, the part of it that relates to physical things, of which the vessel is made
three levels of the soul: the neshama, intellect, in the brain; the ruach, emotion, in the heart; and the nefesh, life, in the liver
the somethingness of the light: its ego, its tangibleness, when it seems to be a distinct entity
intending: directing the mind in prayer, to the light and not to the vessel
faith: trusting that G-d will make everything come out for the best, without worrying about the vessel
trust: an opposite avoda, which focuses on the vessel (to be explained later)
garments or fixers: vessels as they transform the light into a particular expression that reaches a lower level, like glasses for the eye
the campaigns, given as an example of why G-d would want to give a person what he asks for

sections.title: The nimshal: the light of chachma before the vessel is like the soul's intellect before the brain
sections.summary: The light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, as it comes from *Adam Kadmon*, is like the soul's power of intellect before it goes into the brain: one with its source, like the fire inside the coal. What comes out is only like the color of an apple, a separate sign of the essence.

phrases.he: (כח) והנמשל מדוגמא זו
phrases.en: The *nimshal* from this comparison of the way the soul goes into the body

phrases.he: הוא בבחינת ג' כלים דמוחא ולבא כו'
phrases.en: the *nimshal* for this are the three vessels of the brain, the heart and the liver of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: בדרך כלל על כל פנים
phrases.en: at least in general, that's the general idea

blocks.text:
The *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) of the comparison of the way the soul goes into the body. This is interesting, because *dugma* (a likeness) really means an example. So it seems to be a much closer thing: the way your soul goes into your body is *mamash* (literally) the same thing as what he is talking about, just in a smaller way.

The *nimshal* is the three vessels of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation). The three main vessels of *Atzilus* are called **the brain, the heart and the liver**, **at least in general, that's the general idea**.

phrases.he: דאור החכמה דאצילות מצד אצילותה מעצמות אור המאציל,
phrases.en: the light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, the way that it's originally emanated from the *Atzmus* of the light of the *ma'atzil*

phrases.he: הרי זה כאור השכל הרוחני עצמו
phrases.en: like the spiritual power of *sechel*

phrases.he: שנמשך מעצם כח החכמה שבבחינת עצמות הנפש
שמתאחד הוא עדיין במקור חוצבו ממש
phrases.en: that there it's totally one with its source

blocks.text:
The light of *chachma* (wisdom) of *Atzilus*, the way it is originally emanated from the *Atzmus* (G-d's essence) of the light of the *ma'atzil* (the one who emanates): as far as it comes out just as a *gilui* (revelation) of G-d. (Generally *Adam Kadmon* is called the *ma'atzil*.)

Basically, all the levels before *Atzilus*, all the way down to the lights of *Atzilus*, are like the soul. *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man; the first world) and the like are like the soul before it comes into the body. So the essential light of *chachma*, the way it comes out from *Adam Kadmon*, is just like the soul's power of *sechel* (intellect) before it goes into the brain: **the spiritual power of sechel**, which comes from the essence of the power of *chachma* in the essence of the soul.

There it is **totally one with its source**, before it comes into your body. It is just you, and you do not see it as a thing separate from you, that you have this power. You do not recognize the *sechel* as a separate thing yet. Only when it comes into the body and the brain does it become revealed as its own thing, intellect. Right now you just see the soul.

phrases.he: כשלהבת כו'
או גם כגלוי הרצון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: or like the *ratzon*

phrases.he: מעצם הרצון דבחינת אדם קדמון

blocks.title: The flame and the coal
blocks.text:
The real existence of the *sechel* is just revealing you. The way we see the *sechel* is like the flame as it comes outside of the coal: its *gilui*. But there is also the way it is hidden, which is its real essence, like the fire burning inside the coal, and there you do not see it.

So too, there is just a person, and he has this power of consciousness, this power of intellect, a certain genius to him. It is just there in his soul, inherently. What we see is only a revelation of it, seen as if it were separate from the soul, the way it reflects through the body.

**Or like the ratzon**, the essential *ratzon* (will) of *Adam Kadmon*, as was said about the *ratzon l'ratzon* (the will for the will). The inner will of *Adam Kadmon*, before it comes out, is really for yourself: you want to express yourself. Since essentially you have *sechel*, you want to reveal yourself through *sechel*, by being wise. And the particular things, like the desire to help a lady across the street, just reflect your inner desire to be kind. Since according to the circumstances you realize that this is kind, you have a *ratzon l'ratzon* for that thing. But what you essentially want is not its *pratim* (details).

phrases.he: הגם שזהו כמו מראה וגוון בלבד,
phrases.en: even though this relationship is only like an appearance and a color

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב למעלה בענין קורא הדורות מראש
phrases.en: like explained before about the calling it *meirosh*, up in the beginning

phrases.he: שזהו עשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: which is the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שיצאו מהעלם דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: which go out from the hidden of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שהוא גילוי רצון בדבר נבדל כו'
בסוף אות הי"ט)
phrases.en: explained at the end of *os* 19

blocks.text: **Even though this relationship is only like an appearance and a color**: the revelation that comes out is just a totally separate, limited thing, which has no real connection to the *etzem* (essence).

blocks.title: The color of an apple
blocks.text:
The color of an apple tells you whether it is ripe or not. When it is green it is not ripe, at least for red apples, and when it turns red it is ripe. The inside should be white, and that tells you it is sweet; if the inside is brownish, it means it is not. But those colors are not connected to the essential sweetness. They are just a separate thing that reveals it. The essential sweetness is there inherently, regardless of the color you see.

So too, a person is essentially smart before he shows it by solving some problem or doing something. He just has it in his soul, that potential; it is there. What you see is just some external way of revealing it, expressing it.

As explained before about calling it *meirosh*, up in the beginning (*kore hadoros meirosh*, He calls the generations from the beginning), **which is the ten sefiros of Atzilus**, which go out from the hidden of *Adam Kadmon*: the revelation of will in a separate thing, as explained at the end of section 19.

sections.title: Still sefiros b'li ma: once G-d chooses the color, it becomes essential
sections.summary: The lights of *Atzilus* are still undefined, *b'li ma*, because a color that is only a sign becomes bound to the taste, as wanting to help this person becomes bound to being a nice person. In *Adam Kadmon* G-d chose to be wise, a creator and a master, and so these became G-dly attributes, in themselves no more a praise than "all-stupid".

phrases.he: עם כל זה
phrases.en: nevertheless

phrases.he: נקרא עשר ספירות בלי מ''ה, בלי מהות עדיין
phrases.en: the lights are still called the ten *sefiros* without *ma*, *b'li ma*: they're not defined

blocks.text: **Nevertheless**, the lights are still called the ten *sefiros b'li ma* (*sefiros* without a what): **they're not defined**, even the *gilui* of them, when it comes out.

phrases.he: כי כמו שהגוון הוא גם כן עצמי,
phrases.en: but in a way this is also essential

phrases.he: שאי אפשר להיות גוון היפוכו לדבר בעצם
phrases.en: It's impossible to have an opposite color for it

phrases.he: כגוון התפוח בלובן, להורות על עצם טעם המתיקות שבו
phrases.en: like the whiteness of an apple on the inside, which shows the sweetness of it.

blocks.text: The lights that come out now are just the *gilui*: the lights of *Atzilus* are just the *gilui* of *Adam Kadmon*, like the will to help the old lady across the street in the *mashal* (analogy), or like the color of the apple. In a way that is already a thing separate from the essence, **but in a way this is also essential**. **It's impossible to have an opposite color for it**: even though it is circumstantial that this color should mean sweetness, now they are inextricably bound to each other. That's the way it is. The apple has to be this color if it has that taste, **like the whiteness of an apple on the inside, which shows the sweetness of it**.

phrases.he: וכן אור השכל ורצון מטה כלפי חסד,
phrases.en: and similarly if a person has this desire or this direction in his intellect and his desire that leans towards kindness

phrases.he: גם שהוא בענין נבדל,
phrases.en: even though this is in a very specific, detailed thing

phrases.he: מאחר שהוא מורה על העצם כו'

blocks.text: **And similarly**: a person has a desire, a direction in his intellect and his desire, **that leans towards kindness** in a particular situation. He wants to do a nice thing, and his *sechel* looks at it in a nice way, and that reflects the fact that he is a nice person. **Even though this is in a very specific, detailed thing**, once it is understood that this is a nice thing, even though it is circumstantial, a nice person has to look at it this way and want to help this person. You cannot say, "Oh, I'm a nice person, but I don't want to help people, and I don't look at people with a good eye." Then you are not a nice person, even though it is being reflected in something separate.

blocks.question: Why did we use that example of the apple's color?
blocks.text:
The color is not directly connected to the taste at all; it just symbolizes it. So too the fact that you want to do a nice thing in this particular instance. That is harder to see, because seemingly you are a nice person regardless of whether you want to do nice things: "What does the fact that I want to help this person have to do with what I am? Let's say I'm a nice person, and I'm just not showing it." That is possible only until the two things become associated, by *Adam Kadmon*. Once they are associated, if you want to be a nice person you have to do these kinds of things, and then it is an essential thing. That is the whole idea of the *ratzon l'ratzon*: it *mamash* becomes associated.

All this is the *mashal*. What we are really talking about is G-d: going from *Adam Kadmon* to *Atzilus*.

What does that mean? *Adam Kadmon* is where G-d chose the general way He is revealed: His image, His self-image for how He is going to be revealed in the world, His essential character. He chose to reveal Himself through ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), and that is really not for any reason. Therefore nothing He does has to be for a reason; it is that way just because He wants to be that way.

So all the *inyanim* (matters) in *Adam Kadmon* are like the idea of *sechel*. G-d is higher than the limitations of intellect and of a system, but because He chooses that there should be a system, there is a system, and it becomes a real thing. If He chooses to be that way, it *mamash* can be. *Adam Kadmon* is the source of nature and all these kinds of things.

G-d chose to reveal Himself through being logical and all these kinds of things, but you see it as being by His choice. That is the real essence of the *sefiros*, the way they connect to G-d: G-d wants to reveal Himself as being wise. Really He is above the whole thing of wisdom, but He wants it nevertheless to come in a way that will make sense to the intellect and be appreciated. And the same with creation: He wants to reveal Himself through creating everything. G-d is choosing to make these things G-dly attributes. That is the point: within *Adam Kadmon* you see that G-d is choosing to reveal Himself through these things, but inherently they are not connected to Him any more than anything else.

Why should these attributes be G-dly attributes? We say all these things: "G-d's omnipotent and omniscient and omnificent." When can we say that? Only after *Adam Kadmon*. Before that we cannot say that He is all-knowing, or that He is able to create infinitely, because G-d is way beyond the idea of intellect and of a creator. "To Him, you know, it's not any more of a praise to say that He's all-knowing than it is to say that He's like all-stupid." There is no difference. Being able to create infinitely is not essentially a praise to Him. So why should it be a G-dly attribute, that we see G-dliness in His being a creator?

*Adam Kadmon* is where G-d chose a *ratzon* of a *ratzon*. The essential will is that G-d wants to reveal His essence in the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), in the lower world. Then He connected that essential will to the particular wills of the *sefiros*: that He wants to reveal Himself through His wisdom; through having a logical system; through creating everything, and in a way that it appears independent; through miracles and *tzaddikim* (the righteous); through providing everything with its needs and sustenance; through making the world seem to have a system, able to run on its own, self-sufficient; through showing individualized attention over everything; and through creating the limitations of time and space for everything. Those are the ten *sefiros*. And He is the *Malchus* (kingship): He decided that He wants to reveal Himself as the master, who controls everything.

So now, once G-d decided that this is going to be a G-dly attribute, G-d has to control everything. Now G-d has to want to control earthworms, tell them what to do and impose His dominion on them, because now that proves His G-dliness. Essentially it does not, but now that G-d chose it, it becomes intrinsically bound to it.

We have to realize that G-d really could have made it that He would let you create some stuff, and He would not be the creator of everything. He made it that He has His hands in every single thing, creating it every single moment, and that is the way He proves His G-dliness to us.

The creating is the *chesed* (kindness) of *Adam Kadmon*. That G-d creates everything every single moment is the light that comes out after *Adam Kadmon*, the light of *Atzilus*. That is just a *gilui*, like a color, which reveals the essential thing: that G-d chose to reveal Himself as a creator. And once G-d chose to reveal Himself as a creator, it automatically becomes essential for Him to create everything, and He has that will now in an infinite way. It becomes an infinite thing.

sections.title: The lights come from the essential letters: the Names of Adam Kadmon
sections.summary: Because G-d chose a form to reveal Himself in, the letters of *Adam Kadmon*, the infinite lights of the ten *sefiros* come to be: *Ayin Beis*, a *milui* of *yuds*, sees every particular as a real piece of the whole, and *SaG*, with its *alef*, appreciates G-d by comparing. Like the lowest level of the soul's form, these Names work like a function: once G-d chose them, the world has to run in a certain order.

phrases.he: ולכך כל התהוות אורות דעשר ספירות
phrases.en: therefore the whole creation of the lights of the ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: הן באים מבחינת אותיות עצמיים דמאצילן
phrases.en: come from the letters, the essential letters of the *ma'atzil*, from *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: Therefore the whole creation of the lights of the ten *sefiros* comes **from the letters, the essential letters** of the *ma'atzil*, from *Adam Kadmon*. What does that mean? As was said before: G-d chose to reveal Himself in a certain form, which is the letters of *Adam Kadmon*, and that creates the whole idea of these lights of *Atzilus*, of the ten *sefiros*. The infinite lights that are behind the ten *sefiros* are created only once G-d chooses to associate Himself with certain ideas.

Since G-d chose to associate Himself with wisdom, that creates the infinite light: that G-d is expressed through everything having wisdom in it, so that the wisdom found in everything will reveal G-d. Once that is connected to Him, it makes this big will that everything has to have wisdom in it, to reveal G-d. It takes on the G-dly qualities of being essential. It becomes like an axiom, something infinite, with all those qualities: the lights of the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: וכמו שם ע''ב,
phrases.en: for example the name *Ayin Beis*

phrases.he: שממנו בא בחינת אור החכמה דאצילות בגילוי

blocks.text:
**For example the name Ayin Beis** (seventy-two), the Name of *chachma*: G-d chose to reveal Himself through it, to reveal Himself as being wise. And hidden in the way the Name of *Ayin Beis* is spelled is a hint of the form of *chachma* that G-d created: not just that He associated Himself with wisdom, but that He also chose what wisdom is going to be, and that is defined by the Name of 72.

How that is, Rabbi Walters says, he does not understand the symbolism well enough to give a real, great definition of wisdom based on it.

But the general idea of it is that it is a *milui* (the spelling out of a letter's name) of *yuds*. G-d made the general form that everything in creation follows, the form of man, which is expressed by the four letters *yud*, *kei*, *vav*, *kei*: everything has *tzimtzum* (contraction), *hispashtus* (spreading forth), *hamshacha* (drawing down) and *hispashtus*. That is the general form G-d chose to reveal Himself through.

Within that He created the idea of wisdom, which is that there is a *milui* of *yuds*. You see the *tzimtzum*, the *hispashtus*, the *hamshacha* and the *hispashtus*, but you see everything in the way of *tzimtzum*, like the *yud*, the first thing, which is just the *nekuda* (a point). That means you see everything as just a little example representing a bigger *klal* (the whole). Look at anything, and you see that its real existence is that it is a little *prat* (a particular) representing the *klal*.

blocks.title: The child, a piece of the father
blocks.text:
But it is an actual piece of it, like the drop of the father's brain in a child: the child is actually a piece of the father, and therefore he has all the qualities of the father. So too we see everything in the world as *mamash* an actual example. When the idea of *chachma*, which corresponds to the way of *Atzilus*, is revealed, then eating an apple in the way of *chachma* is an actual example, though very small and contracted, of the idea of *chesed*, of getting life, of the power to give life. The experience of getting energy from eating is an actual experience of the *mahus* (what a thing is in itself) of the power to give life.

So you see that essential thing in a very contracted way, as a small example: you see everything as little examples of G-d Himself. That is the idea of *chachma* that G-d created, through which He wants to reveal Himself, and that creates the light of *Ayin Beis* of *Atzilus*: the will that everything should, in an infinite way, express this kind of relationship.

*Chachma* means seeing something as directly connected to the *klal* it represents, until you see it as *mamash* synonymous with it, as actually having a small taste of the *mahus* of the thing. It becomes totally transparent to what it expresses.

Say you appreciate the wisdom in music. What does it mean that you see a big wisdom in it? That you *mamash* get a little taste of a person's talent; you *mamash* see it in the thing. Or a wise person, who can give good advice: he appreciates the way life works, because he had a lot of experience, and in his experiences he saw a lesson about the nature of reality, and he can see how it is really the same as what you are going through. That is the main thing of wisdom: seeing a *prat*, and being able to derive the *klal* from the *prat*.

blocks.title: One piece of chocolate
blocks.text:
You see the *prat* as *mamash* an example, a *dugma* of the *klal*. Even though it is just a symbolic example, it actually contains the whole, like the *Mishna* has the whole *Gemara* in it. That is the level of *chachma*: it comes in a very *kitzur* (shortening), but it has everything in it. Once you taste one piece of chocolate, you have experienced chocolate; every chocolate is the same. Even though you tasted just one piece, you recognize that you had the essence of chocolate, and it is the same for everything. In *chachma* something is an actual example of the essence, and so the whole thing is there, as opposed to learning about it indirectly, like a *mashal*, which does not really have everything.

So G-d created such a relationship: in *chachma* you see everything as a small piece of G-d, a little example of Him in all different ways. That is the idea of the beginning of the *chachma* of *Atzilus*, in revelation.

phrases.he: הרי זה
phrases.en: so that's like the way that the name represents that

phrases.he: שם המורה על עצם דחכמה דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: So the name *Ayin Beis*, the name 72 represents the essential name of *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: וכן שם ס''ג המורה על עצם אור דבינה דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: and the same thing with the name of 63, which represents the essential light of *bina* of *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: **So that's like the way that the name represents that**: the actual letters represent that G-d chose to reveal Himself through that kind of a name. The Name *Ayin Beis*, 72, represents the essential name of *chachma* of *Adam Kadmon*: G-d's choice to be wise and what that means, the picture G-d has of how He wants to reveal Himself as being wise. And from that comes the light of *chachma*.

**And the same thing with the name of 63**, *SaG*, which represents the essential light of *bina* (understanding) of *Adam Kadmon*: G-d chose to reveal Himself through *bina*. It is almost the same as *chachma*, except that in the middle, in the *hamshacha*, there is an *alef* instead of a *yud*. That means you see the essential point, but through a relative thing. You see G-d's greatness by comparing Him to other things; you appreciate the point by comparing how it weighs against a lower point. The *alef* is made kind of like a scale, two points with a line in the middle, to make a distinction between them, to compare them and contrast them. So it is appreciating G-d's greatness by seeing the difference between G-d and creation, and how He is even greater than them: if He can create this, then for sure He must be greater. It is appreciating the essence through something else.

phrases.he: והן ע''ב ס''ג כו' שלפני עשר ספירות דאצילות,
phrases.en: so these names 72, 63, 45 and 52, the names of *Adam Kadmon*, which are before the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: ונקרא שמות המאציל כו'
phrases.en: those are called the names of the Emanator.

blocks.text: These Names, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, 72, 63, 45 and 52, are the Names of *Adam Kadmon*, **which are before the ten sefiros of Atzilus**. **Those are called the names of the Emanator**, *shmos hama'atzil*: just the way G-d chose to reveal Himself.

phrases.he: וכמו בחינת האחרונה שבצורה הרוחניות
phrases.en: this is like the most external level of the spiritual form

phrases.he: שמקושר אל תחילת התהוות האור והצורה בכלי החומר כו'
phrases.en: which is connected to the beginning of the creation of the light and the form in the vessel when it comes into actual matter

blocks.text:
**This is like the most external level of the spiritual form**, which is connected to the beginning of the creation of the light and the form in the vessel when it comes into actual matter, as was said before. As the soul goes into the body, and develops and grows, so the body develops and grows, and the body has to be made in a way that will fit the soul. The eye is made especially to be a vessel for seeing, and the brain for understanding. Since there is already a certain form to the concept of seeing, when it comes into the physical world it has to come in certain ways; it already has a certain definition.

So too, there is a certain definition to wisdom. When you want to express it in the circumstances of our world, even though those circumstances are totally separate from wisdom, when you put the two together it is like a function, and it has to come out with certain kinds of products. Once you have the input and the function, the product is automatic.

blocks.title: Input, function, product
blocks.text:
*Adam Kadmon* is like making a function: setting up a certain system of how you want to interface yourself with the world. Now when you get certain stimuli from the world, you just plug them into your *Adam Kadmon*, and the result is essential; it has to come out with a certain result. Once you have made a certain definition of how you want to reveal yourself, as being kind or as whatever kind of person, when you come to a certain situation you have to act in a certain way that reflects it, or else you are not being who you want to be.

So too, once G-d chose to reveal Himself through a certain thing, the world has to work a certain way in order to reveal G-d. Certain things will reveal Him and certain things will not, and therefore the world runs in a certain order: because G-d chose to reveal Himself through a certain order.

Of course, since He has choice, He can always change things. But as long as you are working within the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), there is a level where it is like a system. That is the basis for why things seem natural, and, on a higher level, for the idea of being able to know what G-d wants, like astrology.

blocks.title: The astrologer and the hammer
blocks.text: Astrology is really a Jewish wisdom: when you know the names of G-d, you understand what G-d wants, and when you see certain things going on in the world, you know how to plug that into the names and figure out what G-d would want to do. Seeing the stars set up in a certain way is like seeing a person take out a hammer. As the *goyishe* (gentile) astrologers say, "Well, if I see a hammer, probably he's going to bang in a nail." Or, to be more correct, since maybe he is pulling a nail: "Oh, so I see something with a nail." They will probably be right most of the time, because that is a very general statement and usually true. But he could be using the hammer for something totally different that has nothing to do with a nail. That is why they will be right only in general, and sometimes totally wrong.

blocks.text: Those are the tools through which He does things. Before the final product comes out, G-d gets out the tools to do different things. So when you see things in the world turning a certain way, the weather is a certain way, all of a sudden a certain guy goes into power, or the stock market takes a turn, and you are not sure how the events will unfold, you could guess the general way things usually go. It is like the weathermen who try to predict the weather: they are usually right in general, sometimes they are totally wrong, and they can only give general predictions. But if you understand what G-d wants to accomplish, which is knowing the names behind the vessels, you will be able to see exactly what He wants to do. If you knew what a person wanted to do and then saw him take out the tool, you would know what he was going to do with it.

No, not in a mechanistic, deterministic way. Even the weather is not mechanistic and deterministic like that. And when they would look in the stars, it does not just mean they would look at the stars. It means they would look at the way things are turning, all kinds of things, everything: the way they would interpret events.

blocks.title: The hurricane that would not hit Florida
blocks.text:
When the weather people see a hurricane coming towards Florida, they say it is probably going to hit Florida full force, so evacuate, and they tell people to evacuate. The Rebbe understands that for whatever reason G-d would not, in that situation, want the hurricane to hit that place, and so the Rebbe said, "You don't even have to bother evacuating, it's not going to happen." The Rebbe understood what the purpose of it was, and saw that the purpose of this hurricane could not be for that to happen.

The truth is that by the Rebbe it is even higher than that; it is not even that the Rebbe figured it out in that kind of a way. By the Rebbe, he is *mamash* in on the plan of what is going to happen. The Rebbe can decide what is going to happen.

But even a regular kabbalist or *tzaddik*: you do not even have to be on that level to be able to know such things sometimes. It is impossible for something to happen, because it is not in G-d's plan; G-d wouldn't do that, it could not be that G-d would want that to happen. So even if, based on the vessel, it looks like that is what is going to happen, you know that if it does not match the name, it is not going to happen.

It is like a person you know is a nice guy who cares for you. If he is doing something that looks like it is against your benefit, you know there is no way he would do something like that, and you can trust that it is not what he is going to do, even though it could look like it. The name means the expression of yourself. If you understand what G-d wants to express, you see what is going to happen.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בדם הוא הנפש
phrases.en: Like we said before, about how the soul goes into the blood

phrases.he: ובצמיחה הרוחנית
phrases.en: and like the spiritual growth going into the physical growth

phrases.he: ובעין ומוח כו'

blocks.text: **Like we said before, about how the soul goes into the blood**, **the spiritual growth going into the physical growth**, and **the eye and the mind**: according to the spiritual form of these powers, the physical form has to work in a certain way to be able to be a vessel for that power. That is only because the spiritual power already has a certain form. Before the spiritual power got that form, in theory, it could work without having to be in that form.

Really, our brain is set up like a really complicated computer, a vessel for thinking. But if G-d wanted to make things a little different, He could make it that a mushy blob of clay would be a good vessel for thinking. But He didn't. "Although, yeah, He kind of did, our brain kind of is this mushy blob." "It is really a joke that the brain thinks. Yeah, the brain really is stupid. It's just this wet slop, this wet, mushy slop."

The spiritual form gets connected to the shape of the vessel, like the cat: whatever it eats turns into a cat, because its soul imposes the cat form onto it. When you eat, you make everything you eat into you. As was said about the blood and the growth: the spiritual form of growth makes the physical form of the tree. And the spiritual form of seeing makes the eye into a vessel that can see, and the power of thought makes the mind into a vessel that can think.

sections.title: The vessel: chachma in the brain of Atzilus, a separate power called wisdom
sections.summary: The vessel that limits the light of *chachma* is like the intellect already blended into the brain, which gets only the thickening of its end. In the vessel, G-d's inherent relationship to everything becomes "wisdom", a power we can name and point to, like the Torah; to define G-d by such attributes is what makes the philosophers' question of evil.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת הכלי המגביל האור דחכמה דאצילות,
phrases.en: However, the vessel that limits the light of *chachma* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: הוא כמו אור השכל שממוזג כבר בחומר המוח
phrases.en: That's like the way that the *sechel* already goes into the brain.

phrases.he: שחומר המוח מקבל רק מהתעבות סוף אור השכל
phrases.en: that the brain only gets the thickening of the end of the light of the intellect.

blocks.text: Now we are talking about the *nimshal*. G-d wanted to reveal Himself in a certain way, which is the spiritual form, and that imposes the form on the world, to be a fitting vessel to reveal it. **However, the vessel that limits the light** of *chachma* of *Atzilus* is like the intellect already blended in the matter of the brain: **the way that the sechel already goes into the brain**.

**The brain only gets the thickening of the end of the light of the intellect**, the *hisabus*. Only the part of the intellect that relates to physical things can be expressed in the brain. There is a certain level where the spiritual concept of intellect can be represented by patterns, which can then be expressed by different orders of neuron flashes and things like that. The way your power of intellect goes into your brain is like the way the light of *chachma* goes into the vessel of *chachma* of *Atzilus*: the vessel is like the brain, and the light is like the soul's power of intellect.

phrases.he: על כן מגבילו,
phrases.en: therefore it limits it

phrases.he: מלבד שינוי המהות כו'
phrases.en: besides changing its *mahus*

phrases.he: כך הוא אור החכמה כשמתלבש במוחא, ונקרא חכמה מוחא כו'
phrases.en: So too, the light of G-d's wisdom when it goes into the vessel called *mocha*, the brain of *Atzilus*, and then it's called *chachma mocha*

blocks.text:
**Therefore it limits it**, **besides changing its mahus**. **So too, the light of G-d's wisdom** when it goes into the vessel called *mocha*, the brain of *Atzilus*: then it is called *chachma mocha*. It becomes limited, and it changes its *mahus*.

Really, *chachma* the way it is in *Adam Kadmon* is the idea that everything is G-d, that the whole relationship of the world is that G-d is just revealing a little example of His being. Then in *Atzilus* G-d chose to reveal His *chachma* through a certain vessel. Really everything is G-d's *chachma*: the most essential description of *chachma* just given could be applied to everything in the world. But G-d wanted His *chachma* to be revealed in certain things and not in other things, so that we will see certain things as being *chachma* and certain things as being *chesed*: a distinction.

So G-d created the idea, not really the Torah yet, just the *chachma* of *Atzilus*: a certain idea of what will be divine wisdom, that certain things will be logical and graceful, with patterns and a reason. When G-d reveals Himself in that, G-d becomes like a super intellect. It is a G-dly intellect, but it becomes a thing that relates to what we call intellect, a limited thing. Now it is seen as wisdom, and not as a revelation of G-d. Instead of being something inherent in everything, it is a thing: G-d has this ability to make things in a way of wisdom. Look into the world and you see that G-d made the world with a certain form; you see G-d's wisdom in the world, His power to make things in the most perfect, beautiful way.

That is already different from the light of wisdom before it went into the vessel, which was just an inherent truth about G-d: that G-d has a certain relationship with the world because of His being, and so it is a revelation of Him. When it goes into the vessel of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, it becomes this separate power.

blocks.title: A kid spilled the ink
blocks.text:
So you see it as a different *metzius* (existence): you see it as wisdom, not as G-d. G-d is revealing Himself by being wise, but indirectly: He shows that He is great because He can be the smartest of anybody. We see that the wisdom in a tree, or the wisdom in DNA, the way the cells work, is much greater than any human thing we could think up, and so we appreciate that it must have come from G-d. Wisdom is already something seen as severed from G-d, but it is so amazing that it could only have been G-d who did it. The design of the world is so great that we say it must be G-d's wisdom; it could not have been an accident.

If the world were simpler, the way we look at it, we could have said it was an accident: "A kid spilled the ink." But since it is so amazing, we say it must have been G-d who did it. It must have been intelligent, and only somebody as intelligent as G-d could do it.

But really, if you look deeper, it is not even like that. Inherently the world must have been created by G-d, or else it just could not exist: it does not make sense for something to just make itself. Even the whole scenario of having the ink and the paper and spilling it could not start without all these prior things; it already makes all these assumptions. But we are already working under those assumptions and limitations, and so even here it is revealed through the vessel of wisdom.

phrases.he: שאז מצד בחינת כלי החכמה הוא בא בשם מציאות דבר שכל,
phrases.en: So then, because of this vessel of *chachma*, the light becomes something that you can call an intellect.

phrases.he: הנקרא התחכמות דבר מה בפרט
phrases.en: actually coming up with a particular idea

blocks.text: **Because of this vessel of chachma, the light becomes something that you can call an intellect**, that you can define as intellect: you can say that G-d is wise. When we say *Hu hamada v'hu hayodea v'hu hayadua* (He is the knowledge, the knower and the known), and when you can describe G-d as omnipotent, omniscient, omnificent, omnipresent and all those things, those are the vessels of *Atzilus*. It is the same as the soul of a person, which, when it goes into the body, becomes the power of movement and the power of seeing.

But the way the soul is, it is a much higher thing than moving a body and lifting things, or even than thinking and seeing. It is higher than being limited to physical perception and physical thoughts. The soul has a certain form, but it does not relate to these limitations. So too, G-d decided to reveal Himself through the vessel He created, a tool: these limitations, the idea of wisdom and the other ideas. Now He reveals Himself by being the ultimate of these things, by showing how He can use them, the way you show yourself by showing how you can use your brain.
"So, that's how you show your Shmuel-ness, right?" You show your personality and everything. And G-d shows it by showing how He uses the same ten *sefiros*.

sensitivity.publishable: That is how you show who you are: you show your personality and everything. And G-d shows it by showing how He uses the same ten *sefiros*.

blocks.text: But most people define G-d that way: G-d is this being that is omnipotent and omniscient and all those things. Really that is not true. To say that that is G-d is just saying He is a big person. He is much higher than those things; He just chose to express Himself through them. That is not the essential definition of G-d. In fact, in philosophy the main proofs against G-d's existence come from those definitions.

blocks.title: How could a wise G-d create stupidity?
blocks.text:
Because they define G-d in those ways, they have a question: if G-d is the ultimate of wisdom, if that defines what He is, how can there be stupidity in the world? "I don't know if they thought that up"; what they actually say is, if G-d is ultimate good, how could there be evil in the world? But it is the same thing with stupidity: if everything comes from G-d, how could an intelligent G-d create stupidity? It is the same question as how a good G-d could create evil, only it does not bother them as much, because it is not an emotionally bothering question. Nobody cares that much that there is stupidity.

What this shows is that the fallacy is not really about evil. The fallacy is that they define G-d as one of two sides of a coin. The idea of wisdom inherently implies stupidity, so they create the question by defining G-d that way. Once you say that G-d is the ultimate of something relative, His existence inherently implies the opposite, or else He could not exist.

blocks.title: The premise makes the question
blocks.text:
If G-d is the ultimate in wisdom and the ultimate in goodness, you are already assuming the existence of good and bad, and that G-d is the ultimate good. Then you cannot ask how bad can exist: you assumed it before you started defining G-d. The fallacy is in their whole premise. If you define G-d as being only good, you have already accepted a prior axiom, before we can discuss G-d, that there is good and evil: something that exists before G-d. That means evil must be able to exist, because you made G-d's existence depend on both good and evil. So you cannot disprove His existence by the existence of evil.

Their whole way of defining G-d is wrong, and that gives them the question. The real conclusion should not be that G-d does not exist, but that their definition is bad. A logical argument dictates that there must be an intelligent creator; then they define what this creator must be, and from that definition try to show that He cannot exist. That only shows that their definition is flawed, because those claims do not uproot the original proof that there must be a creator.

People often do not realize; they do not know how to use logic. When they come up with a fallacy, they do not know what the problem was, and they can come up with these crazy conclusions without realizing that they are confusing themselves. They think the intellect, the logical system they set up, is an actual real thing that works, because they never had the thought of questioning their axioms, and they do not realize that they choose their axioms based on prior things that could be flawed.

sensitivity.reason: Says of the philosophers who argue against G-d that they do not know how to use logic and come to crazy conclusions.
sensitivity.publishable: When an argument comes to a fallacy, a person may not see what the problem was, and come to strange conclusions without realizing that he is confusing himself. He takes the intellect, the logical system he set up, as an actual real thing that works, because he never questioned his axioms, and does not realize that he chose them based on prior things that could be flawed.

blocks.text: That is the way the human intellect works in the brain. So then you can call it an intellect, **actually coming up with a particular idea**. Before it goes into the vessel of *chachma*, it is just the inherent reality of G-d's relationship to any kind of thing, the way He is because of His inherent nature, that He will relate to any creation in a certain way. Once it goes into the vessel of *chachma*, there is: "Give me an example of your wisdom, G-d." Then you have the Torah: the Torah is particular wisdom that came out from the vessel of *chachma*. Before it went into the vessel of *chachma* of *Atzilus*, you could not have a thing like the Torah, a book with wisdom, particular teachings. It would just be an inherent reality everywhere, a totally pervasive reality, not something you could point at.

sections.title: Three governors and four Names: the vessel is made from the thickening of the light
sections.summary: The heart and the liver are vessels like the brain: G-d's modes of conduct and His sustaining of the world, as emotions are felt in the heart and life works through digestion. These three rulers are the letters of the lights, the four Names of *Atzilus*, made from the light's thickening, as a chair takes the shape of the one who sits and a cup the shape of the wish to drink; that is the light's *yeshus*.

phrases.he: וכן המדות הרוחניים בלבא
phrases.en: the same thing, the spiritual emotions in the heart

phrases.he: והנפש הרוחניות בכבדא כו'

blocks.text: **The same thing, the spiritual emotions in the heart.** G-d creates certain systems of how He is going to relate to the world, certain modes of conduct, being strict and being nice, different roles and systems, and those are the vessel to reveal His different relationships with the world, which are the inherent lights of the *middos* (emotional attributes). And the same with the liver: G-d creates a certain way of sustaining the world, how it has to be constantly built up and maintain its form. Those are like the external emotions, the external relationship of G-d to the world, revealed through the vessel of G-d as the provider of sustenance.

"Oh, we didn't do the *mashal* for our heart?" Those details will come later. Right now he is just saying that when it comes into the vessel, it changes from spiritual to physical. When our emotions go from our soul to the heart, we feel them in a certain way: we experience love in a certain way and fear in a certain way, because they are felt through our heart. And the same with our life: it is expressed through the liver, through digestion, using energy and expelling waste, a certain physical process that gives us our basic life, our body built into a certain form. That is the level of *Asiya* (the world of Action) of the soul, the level of *nefesh*, which influences the body to be built in a certain form: the liver.

It is not only defined by the way it is in the body; it really comes from an inner spiritual power. The whole system of eating, of needing certain nutrients, the way our body works, is totally circumstantial to the soul. The soul just wants the body to be a vessel for it, and pushes it into that form. But the way the body works, the DNA, the blood, the liver, is a much more limited thing, and that limits it. Because of the way your digestion works, the soul is expressed only in certain ways: you can eat only certain things, and the soul will turn only certain things into the body. Why? Because it has to do it through the vessel of the liver, and the liver works in a certain way. As far as the soul is concerned, it could be the soul of a tree, and it would do it in a different way with different things, because it has a different vessel.

phrases.he: והן ענין ג' שליטין לעילה,
phrases.en: these three vessels, the brain, the heart and the liver, are called the three governors above

phrases.he: בחינת ג' כלים כללים לנר''נ דזעיר אנפין דאצילות
phrases.en: These are the three general vessels for the *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama* of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: נשמה, שהוא בחינת מוחין דחכמה ובינה שבזעיר אנפין במוחא,
phrases.en: the *neshama*, which is the intellect, the mind of *chachma* and *bina* of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, goes into the brain

phrases.he: ורוח בלבא כו'
phrases.en: and the *ruach* goes in the heart, and the *nefesh* goes into the liver.

blocks.text: These three vessels, **the brain, the heart and the liver, are called the three governors above**: the three vessels that govern everything. G-d created a certain form for His revelation of the consciousness of G-dliness, which is the brain; a certain revelation of the way He is going to interact with the world, as far as good and bad and showing conscious care and direction, which is the heart; and a certain vessel for providing the basic needs, making the world, its design and maintaining it, which is the liver. Since G-d does those in a certain way, certain things make us conscious of certain aspects of that relationship, and other things of other aspects, and those are the vessels G-d has for those things.

**These are the three general vessels for the nefesh, ruach, neshama** (the three levels of the soul) **of Zeir Anpin** (lit. the small countenance) **of Atzilus**. **The neshama, which is the intellect**, the *mochin* (lit. brains) of *chachma* and *bina* of *Zeir Anpin*, **goes into the brain**; **the ruach goes in the heart, and the nefesh goes into the liver**.

phrases.he: והן האותיות דאורות דאצילות,
phrases.en: these vessels are the letters of the lights of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שזהו ענין ד' שמות ע''ב ס''ג דאצילות כו'
phrases.en: These are the four names *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH*, *BaN* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שנקרא כלים לעשר ספירות דאצילות
phrases.en: these are called the vessels for the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: המגבילים האור ומצמצמו,
phrases.en: that they limit the light, and they contract it

phrases.he: לפי שמהתעבות האור נעשה הכלי,
phrases.en: because the vessel comes from the thickening of the light.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*

blocks.text: **These vessels are the letters of the lights of Atzilus**: **the four names Ayin Beis, SaG, MaH, BaN of Atzilus**. G-d defined His revelation through these four Names, and the letters of each define how that revelation is going to work, so that *chachma* gets a certain definition, *bina* gets a certain definition, and so on. **These are called the vessels for the ten sefiros of Atzilus**. They **limit the light, and they contract it**, so that now G-d reveals Himself through these relationships, **because the vessel comes from the thickening of the light**.
Really G-d could reveal Himself in any way, but since He chose to reveal it in a concrete, specific way, by narrowing it down to that specific thing, that makes the vessel.

blocks.title: The chair and the cup
blocks.text:
The shape of a chair comes from your rear end. You already have a certain form, your body, and so you are comfortable in certain positions. When you make a chair, its shape just takes the fact that you are comfortable in certain ways, that you have a certain shape, and puts that idea into tangible form, and it dictates the form of the chair. Or your desire to drink water: put into the context of the way water and different materials work, it creates the form of a cup. That is why all cups have certain things in common: to be an effective vessel within the limitations of our world, it has to have a certain form, because your desire already has a certain form.

So too, G-d first creates a certain form for the way He wants to reveal Himself, which is the light, like your desire to be comfortable or to drink. Then He creates a certain limitation, the vessel, which is like the way the world works. When the two come together, the light gives a certain form to the matter, to make it a good vessel for it.

So G-d made the soul, and He made physical matter with a certain form. When He put the two together, for the soul to express itself through the physical matter, the matter has to be built into the shape of a body; that is the best way for it to express the soul. Both sides of the coin will be discussed soon, the advantage of the light and the advantage of the vessel, but not in this chapter, he thinks. So these are the letters, the vessels of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, which limit the light, **like it says in Etz Chaim**.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא בחינת הישות של האור,
phrases.en: This is called the ego of the light, the somethingness of the light, the tangibleness of it.

phrases.he: כשנראה לבחינת יש ודבר מה במציאות
phrases.en: when it seems to be like a distinct entity.

phrases.he: כידוע ודי למבין

blocks.text: **This is called the ego of the light, the somethingness of the light, the tangibleness of it**, the *yeshus* of the light: **when it seems to be like a distinct entity**. When G-d reveals Himself in a certain form, and it appears that this is who He is, so that you can define Him by that revelation and say what it is, that is the idea of the vessel. When you can say that G-d is wise, it is because G-d put Himself into a vessel, as if it is a body. That is why they define G-d as omnipotent, omniscient and all these different things: G-d put Himself into the vessel of those things as if it is a body.

Just as "I point to your body and say, oh, that's Shmuel," because your soul is in that vessel, so G-d reveals Himself through these vessels as if that is who He is, and it becomes a *yeshus*. But that is the source of the perception of bad, as was explained a little.

sections.summary: There are two sets of Names, one in *Adam Kadmon* before *Atzilus* and one after it as the limiting vessels; so one who intends the Names should intend their source, the light, and the vessel follows by itself. In prayer this means asking for what G-d wants to reveal, not for the winning ticket: *emuna*, and the way to be *mechaven* in *Shmone Esreh*.

וממילא הוא מכוון בכלי החכמה,
phrases.en: automatically you'll be *mechaven b'kli hachachma*

phrases.he: שיומשך למטה כו' ודי למבין

blocks.text: **Based on this, when somebody intends to the names, you should intend to the source of the light**: what is being said now. Seemingly the main thing is the spiritual revelation, and you should think about that Name, and automatically... When you pray, you should have in mind what G-d is really trying to reveal through the vessel of *chachma*, what G-dly revelation is there, and see past the vessel. You should not ask G-d to make things come out in a certain way. Realize that really it is beyond that, and once you clarify the light G-d is trying to reveal, it will automatically come out properly in the right vessel.

It will impose its form onto the vessel automatically; that is the main thing. And **automatically you'll be mechaven** (intending) **b'kli hachachma**, in the vessel of *chachma*. So if you want to understand the Torah, just try to see past it into the G-dliness behind the Torah, and automatically you will understand the Torah properly. That is why, when you learn Torah for its own sake, you are able to understand it properly: you get the real thing behind it. Once you get a perception of what G-d is trying to reveal and become sensitive to the G-dliness, you are automatically able to put it into the intellect properly and make sure it comes out right, because you know the real goal.

blocks.title: Talking to the ear
blocks.text: When you are talking to somebody, you have to talk to his ear, but his ear is only the external vessel; really you want him to understand. What you should do is focus on making him understand, and automatically you will control your voice so that his ear will hear. That is the way you talk to people: you look at their face and see if they are understanding you, and if not, if it looks like they cannot hear you, you automatically adjust the way you talk to make sure they understand. So automatically, if you are *mechaven* to the light, you will be *mechaven* to the vessel. You do not have to worry about it.

blocks.title: "Could you help me?"
blocks.text: And the same when you go ask somebody for something. There are two ways you can ask. "Could you reach in your pocket and give me like a dollar?" Or, "Could you help me?" And automatically he will do whatever he can to help you, and figure out on his own how to do it.

So when you pray to G-d, you should not really be *mechaven* to ask, "Oh, make me win the Tan Yad auction," "cuz that's the vessel!" You should be *mechaven* to why G-d would want to do that, why He would want to give it to you: because He wants to take care of you, or even more, to reveal G-dliness, so that you will do *mivtzoim* or whatever it is. When you focus on that inner *kavana* (intention), G-d will automatically give you whatever you need to do it, and you do not worry about the vessel, because you do not really care how it comes out. You do not really want the money; you want not to have to worry about *parnasa* (livelihood), so that you can pray and do what you need to do. Start doing that, ask G-d for that and focus on it, and automatically everything will be set up so that you can do it properly.

This is called *emuna* (faith): you just trust that G-d is going to make everything come out for the best, and you do not worry about the vessel; you let Him take care of it. You are just *mechaven* to the inner thing: my job is to do Torah and *mitzvos* and what I am supposed to do, and G-d knows what is best for me and will figure out how to help me. Later he will talk about what is called *bitachon* (trust), an opposite *avoda* (divine service), in which you focus on the *kli* (vessel). But right now we are talking about the different...

phrases.he: והיינו כוונות שמות דח''י ברכות שמונה עשרה
phrases.en: This is the way you should be *mechaven* the names in *Shmone Esreh*

phrases.he: כי הא בהא תליא, משום דשורש הכלים המגבילים משמות דעצמות המאציל, כמו שיתבאר ודי למבין)

blocks.text: **This is the way you should be mechaven the names in Shmone Esreh** (the eighteen blessings): when you pray, you should be *mechaven* to the inner thing. As it says in a discourse, you should not just be asking for a physical thing: when you say the blessing for the year, you should be *mechaven* that G-d should give you a year that is successful in praying and learning. There are places that say you should be *mechaven* *davka* (specifically) to the spirituality of the blessings and not ask for the physical, and other places that imply you are *davka* asking for the physical. Later the opposite will come, that you *davka* ask for the physical thing. But really it is both: first you have to be *mechaven* to the spiritual, and once you recognize that, you can go back to actually asking for the physical. That will come in the next chapter or a later chapter.

Since the vessels come from the light, once you are *mechaven* to the light, the vessels will automatically come out good. That is why, when you nullify yourself more to G-d and to Torah and *mitzvos* and you are doing G-d's mission, He automatically gives you all the blessings and everything good so that you can do it properly. To do it properly you need money, and health, and no worries, and children, and everything like that. So if you are *mechaven* to the *kavana*, G-d will automatically give you those things.

That is the main *kavana* in *Shmone Esreh*, and why it comes after the *Shema*. If in the *Shema* you are *mechaven* to have *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) for G-d, to nullify yourself, to commit yourself to doing Torah and *mitzvos*, to accept the yoke of the kingdom of heaven and the yoke of the *mitzvos*, then G-d answers you in *Shmone Esreh*. When you ask, you are *mechaven* that you want to spread G-dliness, and then you become a good vessel for the light, so G-d wants to give it to you, because it is not a waste. G-d is not going to give you the stuff if it is going to go against the *kavana*; it is a waste. Now really G-d loves us and He will give us things, and there are all kinds of things going on here, but that is the idea of being *mechaven* in *Shmone Esreh*.

sections.title: Tikunim: the eye is the soul's glasses
sections.summary: The vessels are also called *tikunim*, garments that fix: as glasses, a telescope or a microscope fix the eye to see further, the physical eye fixes the soul's power of sight to focus on physical things.

phrases.he: והיינו מה שכתוב וקרינן לון י' ספירין כו'
phrases.en: and this is what it says in *Tikunei Zohar*, that G-d called them ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: לאחזאה לאנהגא כו',
phrases.en: to reveal Himself, and to conduct the world

phrases.he: כי תיקונין הן בחינת הכלים לאורות דאצילות
phrases.en: the garments are the vessels to the lights of *Atzilus*

blocks.text: Here at the end of chapter 28 we are talking about *tikunim* (garments). What is the difference between a *kli* and a *tikun*? This is what it says in *Tikunei Zohar*: **that G-d called them ten sefiros**, **to reveal Himself, and to conduct the world**. It says that G-d brought out ten *tikunim*, ten garments, and called them the ten *sefiros*. So these are called *tikunim*, garments: **the garments are the vessels to the lights of Atzilus**. But it is a little different from what was said before.

phrases.he: וכמו על דרך משל תיקון העין,
phrases.en: for example, like the way that you fix up the eye

phrases.he: שיתפשט ראיה גשמית שבו יותר,
phrases.en: that its physical sight should go further

phrases.he: הוא על ידי אמצעות כלי ההבטה כו'
phrases.en: is through a vessel for seeing, either a telescope or a microscope or regular glasses.

phrases.he: כך תיקון התפשטות ראיה הרוחניות על ידי אמצעות כלי העין הגשמי כו'
phrases.en: So too the physical eye is like the glasses for the soul.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר
phrases.en: as explained elsewhere

blocks.title: Glasses for the soul
blocks.text:
**For example, like the way that you fix up the eye**, **that its physical sight should go further**: it **is through a vessel for seeing, either a telescope or a microscope or regular glasses**. The garments called *tikunim* fix the thing; that is why it is called a *tikun*, as the word means: it helps it do something it could not normally do.

**So too the physical eye is like the glasses for the soul.** It fixes the soul's power of sight so that it can focus on physical things, because really the soul has the power of sight; it just needs something to channel it to physical things. Just as you can really see, and only need something to channel your sight to a very faint, far-away star, or to something very small in a microscope, the eye just channels the power of sight to focus on physical things, like a microscope.

blocks.title: What a telescope does
blocks.text: The only problem is that the lens of your eye does not focus that well; as far as your power of sight, there is no difference. What does a telescope do when you look through it? All it does is make your eye focus on a much smaller point than normal. A lens five inches wide takes however much light hits those five inches and focuses it on your eye, which is a quarter of an inch or less, an eighth of an inch. So you get a lot more light hitting your eye, he does not know, a couple of times more, exponentially, and you can focus on something very faint that you would not normally see, either because it is too small for your eye's resolution to notice the details, or because it has very little light and is too faint.

blocks.title: Pixels per degree
blocks.text: So you can see with a telescope. A microscope does the same idea: it takes something very small and focuses it on your eye. All it does is blow up the image a little, so that your eye can notice the details, because really you could see it. The problem is that your eye has only a certain resolution: "It only has like 288 pixels per degree of vision." Whether they call it 360 or 180 degrees of vision, for each degree you have approximately 288 cells that can see in your main vision, and fewer in your peripheral vision. So depending on how close something is, you can see more and more detail, but eventually something too small just slips in between the pixels of your eyes. If you blow up the image, you can see it. It is no different than anything else; you just have to fix your eye to focus on that kind of a thing.

blocks.question: Are you fixing the eye, or are you fixing the image?
blocks.text: It does not really matter; it is the same thing. "Yeah, in a way, you're right." You are just fixing the image so that it can focus in the eye; it is kind of a two-way thing. On the other hand, the eye is trying to see, and you are refocusing it so that it is able to see. **As explained elsewhere.**

sections.title: Through the limiting vessels the light comes down: kli and tikun
sections.summary: Only in the limiting vessels can the light be drawn down: an idea settled in the mind reaches the emotions and other people, love in the heart reaches a receiver. A *kli* holds the whole power at rest, like the body for the soul; a *tikun* transforms it into one particular expression, like a uniform, so that we can see G-d without being burned. In the essential light the *sefiros* are still *b'li ma*: G-d's wisdom and creating are infinite in everything, and seen in a tree only as a glimmer of a glimmer.

phrases.he: על כן מצד בחינת הכלים המגבילים, על ידי זה דוקא יוכל להיות כל בחינת השפעות והמשכות למטה מטה
phrases.en: Therefore, specifically when the light goes into the vessels that limit the light, it's able to be revealed down to the physical world.

phrases.he: וכמו על ידי כלי המוח שישיג השכל, ימשיכנו להמדות
phrases.en: So therefore, if through the mind grasping the *sechel*, an intellect, it's able to bring it down to the emotions

phrases.he: או להשפיעו לזולתו
phrases.en: or it can be explained to someone else.

blocks.text: **Therefore, specifically when the light goes into the vessels that limit the light, it's able to be revealed down to the physical world.** So, **through the mind grasping the sechel**, **it's able to bring it down to the emotions**, **or it can be explained to someone else**. For you to be able to explain something, even to yourself, to bring it to an emotional feeling or to somebody else, it has to be brought out in an inner way, so that you actually understand it well. You can have something in the way of *emuna*, where you feel it, but it did not really settle into the vessel of your mind. When it settles in the vessel of your mind, you can bring it down to yourself or to someone else.

That is one of the main things of learning *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching). A Jew has this essential *emuna* in G-d, but through studying it you are able to bring it to affect you emotionally and in your actions, and to affect other people with it. That happens only when it goes into the *kli*; otherwise the light is not fixed, and you do not know how to focus it into an emotional response or into actions. You can believe in G-d, but you do not know what to do about it unless you learn the Torah and understand that this is what G-d wants you to do, and therefore you should do this and not that. And even the idea itself of believing in G-d: you have to understand what it means for the way you relate to the world.

blocks.question: How can the soul see without the eye?
blocks.text: It is just not a physical sight. You are used to physical sight, so that is what you call sight. But the real idea of sight does not have to be what you call sight: it is being able to perceive an essence directly. The way the soul is in the Garden of Eden, it perceives G-dliness in a way of *re'iya* (sight). And you see in yourself that you can dream without your eye, and see things. So you do not really need your eye to see. The eye just triggers the first perceptions, because it contracts the *koach* (power), but the *koach* is really in you before that.

blocks.question: Well, you still need your brain?
blocks.text: That is not really true. You are only used to being conscious within your body; "I'm also, I can't, I don't know what it's like to be just a soul." But just as you do not need your eye, you do not really need your brain either. And not only that: when the soul goes up and leaves the body, it still carries its memories of the world with it. What is a real example? The example they give is the Garden of Eden, "but, you know, who knows about that."

The way it is before it goes into the *kli* is the *mashal* for before *Atzilus*, and it is the same in G-dliness. Before *Atzilus* the lights of G-dliness are all hidden, just as your soul is a hidden thing before it goes into your body. They are the essential lights of G-d, which you cannot really know: it is already a thing of *ilu yedativ hayisiv* (if I knew Him, I would be Him), totally infinite. That is why the *mashal* is a soul before it goes into the body: how can you really know what it is? Even our own soul we do not really know. We have no *hasaga* (comprehension) of the *mahus* of our own soul; we have it only through our body. That is the way we understand it.

Just as our soul is hidden when it is not in our body, so too G-dliness is hidden when it is not in the vessels of *Atzilus*, to the point that it is called *Radla*, the head that does not know: it does not even know what it is. It is not revealed, and it is not yet a known thing.

blocks.question: We already know it is a hidden thing; what is there to know about it?
blocks.text: That is exactly what it is: a hidden thing, and that is exactly what we are trying to know. We do not want to know what it is as a revealed thing right now; we want to know what a hidden thing is. The *mashal* for the hidden thing is our soul before it comes into the body, and we know what that is: a hidden thing. Right now we are just trying to understand the relationship.

There it is totally hidden, like our soul before it comes into the body. You cannot really even speak of sight yet; it is a totally higher thing, and in a way it has nothing to do with all this. Before it comes to the eye there are dreams, because the eye is obviously just triggering it. But the truth is that even the brain: it must be coming from the soul, "because the brain is just a bunch of dirt." Consciousness cannot be coming from the brain. So even now you are really seeing your soul itself, just through the vessel. When you experience consciousness, you are actually having a *hasaga* of the essence of your soul. That is actually your soul, just as it comes into the vessel of your body; it is *mamash* your soul itself, because only your soul can be conscious.

The *nimshal* for that point: the way G-d reveals Himself in the lights before *Atzilus*, they are just essential lights. They include the ten *sefiros*, but you just appreciate that G-d can do anything and is beyond limitations. So automatically He also has the ability of *chachma*, but you do not see that you can define G-d as wise the way we know it. He is really beyond that; He could also do that, because He can do anything. What you perceive is His essential quality of being infinite, transcending limitations, able to do anything.

Then, when it comes to the vessel of *Atzilus*, G-d expresses His infinite abilities. "Oh, G-d, yeah, can you really do anything?" "Yeah, I can really do anything." "Let's, show me what you can do." "Okay, I can be infinitely wise, and I can be infinitely kind, and create infinitely." Creating something from nothing shows that He can do anything, since only G-d could do it, but it is already shown through a specific vessel. The same with such wisdom: it could only be from G-d.

He did not say that it is only a vessel, but it is: it is like the one vessel of *Akudim*, where ten things are all in one vessel. That is really the idea: that it is all one is like the will, which means that G-d can do whatever He wants, one vessel that includes everything. And that, by the way, is the source of the Jews: we come from the level of that one vessel, which is still *b'li ma*, and not from the particular things. We come from the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought), the one thought that includes everything, which is that general limitation.

Within the *hishtalshelus*, the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will) is to reveal that He can do anything. But revealing that is not the ultimate thing; it is, as it says, *mishleimus koach maasav u'peulosav*, from the perfection of the power of His deeds and actions. As it says here, *l'achzaa*, to reveal Himself to people: that is not the ultimate thing. The ultimate thing is the *dira b'tachtonim*, the revelation of the Essence through our *avoda*. That is the main thing G-d wants: that it should be *davka* through our *avoda*.

phrases.he: וכן על ידי אמצעות כלי הלב לאור האהבה והחסד הרוחני,
phrases.en: the same way that when the light of love and kindness goes into your physical heart

phrases.he: יבא לכלל השפעה למקבל כידוע
phrases.en: then it relates to giving it out to a *mekabel*.

blocks.text: The vessel lets you bring it all the way down to somewhere lower. **The same way that when the light of love and kindness goes into your physical heart, then it relates to giving it out to a mekabel** (receiver). Once it goes into your heart, it becomes a motivation to do certain things and act in a certain way: that is how you express the feelings of love and kindness in the physical world. But those are really physical symptoms, the way your body reacts to love and kindness, wanting to be close and wanting to give. It is not really in the heart, nor in the brain; it comes through there.

Everything really goes through the brain first. That is why it is called *rosh* (head), like *Rosh HaShana* and *Rosh Chodesh*: it includes everything, and from there it divides out. And that is why scientists laugh at the old-fashioned people who used to say that love is in the heart: "Oh, it's in the brain, because we see that if you take out this part of the brain then they don't have emotions." "But they're just haughty idiots," just trying to pump themselves up, "Oh, we know better," instead of trying to understand what is being said. "Oh, it's obvious, everybody knows that it's coming from the brain." It says here that it comes from the brain; everything goes through the brain. Just that then it is revealed in the heart, "and any idiot knows that, that you feel the feeling of love in your heart." It is true that your consciousness works only through the brain, but afterwards you feel it in the change in your breathing and the speed of your heart rate, which you feel in your heart.

phrases.he: ולכך נקרא תיקונין,
phrases.en: Therefore, the vessels are called fixers

phrases.he: כדי שיבא על ידם בחינת המשכה מאצילות לבריאה
phrases.en: through them there's *hamshacha* from *Atzilus* to *Beriya*.

phrases.he: והיינו רק לאחזאה כו'
phrases.en: and this revelation from *Atzilus* to *Beriya* is just to reveal Himself to man and to conduct the worlds.

blocks.text: **Therefore, the vessels are called fixers**, *tikunim*: **through them there's hamshacha from Atzilus to Beriya** (the world of Creation). **And this revelation from Atzilus to Beriya is just to reveal Himself to man and to conduct the worlds.**

phrases.he: אבל מצד עצמות אור המאציל נקרא עשר ספירות בלי מה כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: but the way that they are in the essential light of the *ma'atzil*, they're called the ten spheres without any *mahus*, like I said before

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות:

blocks.text: **But the way that they are in the essential light of the ma'atzil, they're called the ten spheres without any mahus, like I said before**: you cannot really say what they are; they are not that limited.

So basically what he is explaining here is that there are two things in the vessels. First, the inner thing: they are just a place where the soul rests. Your consciousness just rests in your body; your intellect rests in your brain, your emotions in your heart, and your biological life in your liver. That is the inner side of the vessels, when they are called a *kli*: those powers are revealed and rest there. But when you use these things, your brain to think an idea, your heart to feel an actual emotion, your liver to digest food, then the vessels are called *tikunim*, garments or fixers: they take the light and transform it into something that can relate to the physical world, so that you can have an effect.

Your eye fixes your power of sight so that it can see physical things; your brain fixes your consciousness so that it can affect your body and come up with physical ideas; your power of movement can now actually move physical things. Just as your eye is fixed by glasses to see something, so too here the soul is fixed: it is revealed in a limited way that we can perceive, and now we can perceive G-dliness. Now that G-d reveals Himself through these vessels, it becomes a limited thing that we can actually understand and perceive.

The difference is that a *kli* is just the way the light of the soul rests in a thing, as your consciousness rests in your brain; that is just called a *kli*. When it shines through the brain to become physical thoughts, it is called a *tikun*: it does not just hold your soul, it actually helps it come across to a lower level. So the vessels do two things: the light rests in them, and they transform the light into something that can come down to the next level.

Your body is a fitting vessel that lets you be alive; your soul just rests in your body. But your body also lets your soul interact with the physical world. That you can move things is already a *tikun*: your soul now uses your body to relate to the world outside the body, lower than it, even to things that are not a vessel for the soul. There is a big difference: when it rests in the vessel, you *mamash* have the *etzem* there. Not only is it a good vessel; your consciousness actually rests in your body.

So two things are accomplished. An emotion in your heart does two things. First, it limits it so that you are aware of the feeling you are having, a consciousness of a certain feeling, which is just the vessel. Then it also makes it something you can express to someone else. It does both: it does something for you, giving you a defined character, which is what was said before, like names, like giving yourself a name that defines you as a distinct thing; and it lets you relate to other people. First it is just for you, and afterwards it comes out to be able to relate to someone else.

When you understand an idea, you are conscious of it because it came to your physical brain. You do not understand it fully until it goes into your brain and you put it into words; then you are totally conscious of it. Once you have it that way, you can also explain it. But at first you are not necessarily thinking about explaining it; it is just for you, or it could be just for you.

The truth is that the main thing of the *kli* is not a particular expression, but the fact that it can be used for anything. That you are able to think with your brain: that is the *kli*. It is a *tikun* when you actually think a particular thing and it lets you bring it across. It does not let you bring across your power to think; it lets you bring across your particular idea. From the side of the power of thought it is only a vessel; from the side of a particular idea, it brings it across and transforms it into something that can be brought across. When you use your hand to move something, it does not give the thing you move the power of movement, only the particular movement you made. Whereas your hand is a vessel for your power of movement, and so it is infinite: you can move in whichever way you want.
